 Trevon Brazile has big game on boards in NBA debut
 Daniel Fair @ hawgbeat 10/23/26 0 Share Share 
 New members can subscribe to HawgBeat now and get 60% off of your first year! Visit  our homepage  to sign up today to take advantage of this unbeatable offer! This includes not only complete access to HawgBeat, but all On3 and Rivals national content, plus  The Trough premium message board .  
 The NBA season is here, and Trevon Brazile had a game to remember in his first official outing as a member of the Denver Nuggets. 
 The four-year former Razorback, who was drafted in the second round by the Nuggets, had been making waves in the NBA preseason. During the Summer League, it was his scoring that he showed off. But in his NBA debut, it was his rebounding.
 Brazile didn’t have an eye-popping offensive game. He scored his first two NBA points on a pair of free throws and got his first field goal in the third quarter under the bucket off a pass from Nikola Jokic. 
 And there it is! TB's first NBA bucket! 🔥 #ProHogs pic.twitter.com/zprkZ4QGoG 
— Arkansas Men’s Basketball 🐗 (@RazorbackMBB) October 23, 2026 
 Where he did look great was in the rebounding column. He finished with a team-high 12 rebounds, eight of which came within his first five minutes of action on the floor.
 “His rebounding impact is enormous,” Nuggets head coach David Adelman said after the game. “He’s just got special skills…we’re going to need him.”
 Three of those 12 rebounds came on the offensive side of the floor as well. He also committed two fouls and turned the ball over once and finished -1 in the plus/minus, better than all five starters for the Nuggets in their 96-84 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder on Thursday night.
 While he didn’t have the best offensive outing, Nuggets head coach David Adelman said he thought Brazile could have been more aggressive with the ball in his hands. 
 “TB did exactly what he was supposed to do, and I thought he turned down shots,” Adelman said. “I’d love to see him shoot four or five threes a game. He’s got a really nice release.”
 One thing that Adelman talked about with Brazile was that he was ready for the moment of his first NBA game, and he performed despite the lights and glamor of the big stage against a team like Oklahoma City.
 “For a young kid to come in here, OKC, rookie year, first game, national TV, all that stuff, he didn’t seem fazed by it,” Adelman said.
